newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary halts false electricity coupon-share swap.
newsitem.headline: Hungary halts false electricity coupon-share swap.

text.p: Hungary's financial and bourse watchdog (APTF) excluded 485 illegal subscribers from a compensation coupons share swap for electricity company ELMU.
"Out of a 700-strong sample of subscriptions 485 could not be backed up with compensation coupons," Zoltan Pacsi, APTF deputy director, told a news conference on Monday.
State privatisation agency APV Rt offered last November an eight percent stake in electricity company Budapesti Elektromos Muvek (ELMU) primarily to original holders of coupons.
Compensation coupons were awarded to victims of expropriations and persecutions under Hungary's former fascist and communist regimes.

ELMU has a registered capital of 60.78 billion forints, with the German consortium of RWE and EVS holding 46.15 percent, APV Rt 36.33 percent, the city of Budapest 10.13 percent and the rest held by other municipalities.

Earlier press reports suggested that false subscriptions could have been filed on behalf of investors whose aim was to exclude original compensation coupon holders in order to boost the number of shares available for non-preferential subscription.

APV set aside 196,455 shares for domestic original coupon holders, 97,500 for non-resident original coupon holders, 50,000 for coupon investment companies, 95,000 for municipalities and 47,000 for agricultural cooperatives.
Any shares left after these subscriptions were satisfied, would have gone to subscribers who had bought their coupons on the secondary market.
Pacsi said the APTF and APV also decided that the validity of all 10,000 applications will be checked by the issuer of the coupons, Hungary's Compensation Office against existing records.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, compensation coupons closed at 630 forints, down 35, on Monday, .
